name: FinanceBench - Retrieval Accuracy
description: Retrieval benchmark over FinanceBench questions about public-company SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, earnings reports). Models and RAG pipelines are ranked by how often they retrieve the evidence page needed to answer the question.

name: Amazon Reviews - Classification Accuracy
description: Product-review classification on Amazon reviews (Datafiniti). Models are ranked by accuracy at predicting the review label from the review text.

name: RAG Instruct - Answer Accuracy
description: Retrieval-augmented question answering from llmware's RAG Instruct benchmark: each question comes with a context passage, and answers are ranked by exact match against the reference answer.

name: Financial Phrasebank - Classify Accuracy
description: Financial sentiment classification on Financial PhraseBank: label financial news sentences as positive, negative, or neutral. Models are ranked by F1.

name: TREC - Hierarchical Classification Accuracy
description: TREC question classification: assign each question to its answer-type category (e.g. location, number, person). Models are ranked by accuracy.

name: Banking Dataset - Classification Accuracy
description: Banking intent and sentiment classification on short customer and financial texts. Models are ranked by accuracy.

name: ARC-SMART
description: ARC-SMART, a filtered version of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge: grade-school science multiple-choice questions. Models are ranked by accuracy.

name: MMLU-SMART
description: MMLU-SMART, a filtered version of MMLU covering multiple-choice knowledge questions across academic subjects. Models are ranked by accuracy.

name: CommonsenseQA-SMART
description: CommonsenseQA-SMART, a filtered version of CommonsenseQA: multiple-choice questions that require everyday commonsense reasoning. Models are ranked by accuracy.

name: Geolocation Inference - Median Distance Error
description: Geolocation inference: predict where an image or text was captured. Models are ranked by median great-circle distance error in kilometres (lower is better).

name: SST-2 Sentiment (Sample)
description: Stanford Sentiment Treebank binary sentiment classification. 20-sample subset.

name: EnterpriseBench
description: EnterpriseBench tests whether tool-calling LLM agents behave safely on enterprise workflows, not just whether they call the right function. On 16 policy-annotated tasks across eight workflow categories (email, CRM, HR, data pipelines, calendar, documents, IT support, finance), agents are ranked by policy compliance rate: the share of tasks with no policy violation (1 minus the paper's Policy Violation Rate). Automated scoring of new submissions needs a tool-calling evaluator that is not built yet; rows below are the paper's reported results.

models.model: Reference agent (always returns the ground-truth tool call)
models.source: EnterpriseBench paper draft, Section 5.1 (PVR 50% [95% CI 25-75%], 8 of 16 tasks): https://github.com/anote-ai/research-enterprisebench/blob/4632f1c0d3420b8d9de64f4737081b561ce3c06c/PAPER_DRAFT.md
EnterpriseBench paper draft, Section 5.2 (PVR 56% [95% CI 31-81%], 9 of 16 tasks): https://github.com/anote-ai/research-enterprisebench/blob/4632f1c0d3420b8d9de64f4737081b561ce3c06c/PAPER_DRAFT.md

research.seo_description: EnterpriseBench leaderboard: do tool-calling LLM agents follow enterprise policy? Policy compliance of GPT-4o-mini and a reference agent on 16 workflow tasks.
research.paper_title: EnterpriseBench: Do Syntactic Tool-Calling Benchmarks Predict Deployment Trustworthiness?
research.notes: Scores are 1 - PVR from the paper draft; the confidence interval is the paper's PVR interval mirrored. The two agents' intervals overlap, so the ranking is not statistically significant.

name: RetrievalBench (Finance, FiQA)
description: RetrievalBench treats document chunking and embedding-model choice as experimental variables in cross-domain retrieval. This leaderboard shows the finance domain (FiQA: 2,000 documents, 500 queries): every combination of four chunking strategies (fixed-512, sentence, recursive, semantic) and four retrievers (BM25 and three dense embedders), ranked by NDCG@10. In this domain fixed-512 chunking beats semantic chunking by 26-41% relative NDCG@10 for every dense embedder.

name: Financial Document Retrieval (FinanceBench)
description: A seven-condition ablation of RAG retrieval techniques on 133 FinanceBench analyst questions over 10-K, 10-Q and earnings filings: semantic and recursive chunking, cross-encoder reranking, metadata enrichment, HyDE query expansion and a full hybrid, all answering with GPT-4o. Ranked by exact match, counted when the gold answer appears in the model's answer; ROUGE-L F1 is reported alongside because the two metrics rank the conditions differently.

name: Semantic Chunking for FinanceBench QA
description: Does semantic-boundary chunking or a hybrid retrieval pipeline beat plain fixed chunking on financial filings? A controlled three-condition ablation on a stratified 14-question FinanceBench sample, with Claude generating every answer and TF-IDF/BM25 retrieval. Ranked by mean ROUGE-L F1 in Run 1; Run 2, an independent repeat, is shown alongside. Neither enhancement beat the baseline in either run.

models.model: Claude + fixed word-based chunking, TF-IDF (C0 baseline)
models.source: Semantic chunking README 'Ablation Design' table (Run 1 and Run 2 mean ROUGE-L F1): https://github.com/anote-ai/research-semanticchunking/blob/44b4ed55d50b4a8ab5aa3800f6afa394f2f00921/README.md

models.model: Claude + hybrid: structure-aware chunks, BM25/TF-IDF fusion, metadata, HyDE, reranking (C6)
models.source: Semantic chunking README 'Ablation Design' table (Run 1 and Run 2 mean ROUGE-L F1): https://github.com/anote-ai/research-semanticchunking/blob/44b4ed55d50b4a8ab5aa3800f6afa394f2f00921/README.md
Semantic chunking README 'Ablation Design' table (Run 1 and Run 2 mean ROUGE-L F1): https://github.com/anote-ai/research-semanticchunking/blob/44b4ed55d50b4a8ab5aa3800f6afa394f2f00921/README.md

research.seo_description: Semantic vs. fixed chunking on FinanceBench: ROUGE-L of baseline, semantic and hybrid retrieval pipelines for financial document QA across two independent runs.
research.paper_title: Semantic Chunking and Hybrid Retrieval for Financial Document QA: An Ablation Study on FinanceBench
research.notes: 14 questions: enough to catch a large effect, not fine distinctions. C1's shortfall vs. the baseline is significant in Run 1 (95% CI [-0.073, -0.002]); C6's is not significant in either run.

name: AnnotateBench (Financial PhraseBank)
description: AnnotateBench compares annotation strategies under fixed labeling budgets: how much labeled data does each strategy need? This leaderboard shows Financial PhraseBank sentiment classification with a TF-IDF + logistic-regression classifier trained on the labels each strategy selects, reported at each strategy's best budget (500 or 1,000 labels) and ranked by test macro-F1, averaged over five seeds.

name: OrchestraBench Routing
description: OrchestraBench evaluates the orchestration layer of multi-agent LLM systems. This leaderboard is its routing experiment: given a task description, choose decompose, direct_tool, code_execution or reason_only. 26 expert-labelled cases: 16 where surface cues match intent and 10 adversarial cases where they mislead. Ranked by accuracy; submissions are scored automatically against the gold labels.
